## History

The line of descent, oldest first:

- **the halfling proto-language**, 20 kyr ago: the reconstructed ancestor (halfling).
- **Ipohsu (halfling 14, the east of Simath)**, 20 kyr ago: continued the proto-language in place (spoken by halfling).
- **Siyyihhu (gnome 13, the west of Simath)**, 1 kyr ago: formed when the speakers took up another language.

**Shift.** 1 kyr ago the gnome speakers of deme 526 took up the language of the halfling (halfling 14). Trigger: settlements: 96 site(s) of the gnome taken by the halfling about 6.0 kyr ago (a town or city among them) (settlements.json holders).
From the old language (gnome 13) 68 words were kept, mostly landscape, plants and animals: fish, fly (insect), bird, dog, flower, leaf, louse, root, stone or rock, worm, bear, deer, grass, hill, ….
The accent the speakers brought (new sound heard as old): dʒ > s, d̪ > t, kʼ > k, nʲ > n, pʼ > p, tʼ > t, z > s, zʷ > s, ȴ > j, ȵ > ɲ, ȶ > t, ɓ > b, ɛ > a, ɟ > ɡ, ɟʝ > ɲ, ɨ̠ > i, ɹ > n, ɽ > ɾ, ʈ > t, ʒ > s, ʔ > h.
Grammar carried over: definite article none > pre.

**Contact.** Sound changes taken up from neighbours by the wave along the line: gnome 13 (29), gnome 1 (25), human 33 (8), human 33 (5), halfling 32 (5), halfling 28 (5). Loan events in the present vocabulary (by donor): bronze dragon 5 (11), hill giant 8 (7), blue dragon 10 (6), gnome 13 (4), copper dragon 1 (4), halfling 28 (4).

Unrounded vowels come before the dot, rounded after it. Length: no long vowels. Nasality: no nasal vowels.

### Tone, syllables and stress

No phonemic tone.
Syllable shapes (share of syllables in the word-shape model): CV 45%, CVC 25%, CCV 11%, CCVC 8%, V 7%, VC 4%. At most 2 consonant(s) before the vowel and 1 after it.
Stress falls on the first syllable.
Core words average 1.87 syllables (4.3 sounds); 14% of words share their form with another word.

### Allophony

This output records no allophones (the engine stores sounds as phonemes only).

## Orthography

The house romanization in two registers: the full spelling (workbench, one letter or digraph per sound, tone marks) and the book spelling (lossy: no tone, plain vowels, at most one diacritic letter a word).

**Consonants:** m ‹m› · n̪ ‹n̪› ‹n› · n̥ ‹hn› · n ‹n› · ɳ ‹ṇ› · ɲ ‹ny› · ŋ͡m ‹ngm› · ŋ ‹ng› · ŋʷ ‹ngw› · p ‹p› · b ‹b› · t̪ ‹t̪› ‹t› · t ‹t› · d ‹d› · ɖ ‹ḍ› · k ‹k› · ɡ ‹g› · ʔ ‹'› · cç ‹cç› ‹ky› · s ‹s› · ʒ ‹zh› · f ‹f› · v ‹v› · x ‹kh› · ɣ ‹gh› · h ‹h› · j ‹y› · w ‹w› · l̪ ‹l̪› ‹l› · l ‹l› · ɾ ‹r›

**Vowels:** i ‹i› · u ‹u› · e ‹e› · o ‹o› · a ‹a›

Where two spellings are given the second is the book spelling.

## Grammar

Basic word order is SVO; it has prepositions. In the noun phrase: possessed before the possessor; noun before the adjective; noun before the demonstrative; noun before the numeral; noun before the relative clause. Overall it is head-initial.
It has a definite article before the noun, an indefinite article, a few cases, split alignment (ergative in some contexts, accusative in others), no grammatical number, no gender or noun classes.
Verbs mark perfective and progressive; there is an indirect (reported or inferred) evidential. Negation uses a negator before the verb; yes/no questions use intonation alone. Verbs agree with the subject by prefixes; not with the object.
Other features: serial verbs; a bound causative; no passive; question words moved to the front; a decimal counting base; a 'have' verb for possession.
Note on the data: the typology features and the live markers disagree here (number is 'none' but a plural or dual marker is live (PL)). Both are shown as recorded.
Measured morphology: 6 live grammatical markers, mean bondedness 0.8 (0 free word … 3 fused), 4 paradigm cells, 0 of them with allomorphy.
